items.title: When police charged an NRL star, one detective broke ranks
items.description: As the footballer, shirt torn, face bloodied and with a concussion, paced his police cell, a veteran detective's phone started to ring.

items.title: Iranian media reports peace talks with US halted, as Trump says they continue at 'pace'
items.description: Iranian state media is reporting that the country's government has halted negotiations with the United States over an end to the war in the Middle East, in protest over Israel's conduct in Lebanon.

items.title: Even Pauline Hanson knows polling isn't everything
items.description: The One Nation leader, whose popularity has soared in the past 12 months, would be the first to say she doesn’t put too much stock in the numbers.

items.title: Could the battery boom lower inflation and interest rates?
items.description: Fossil fuels, which have powered the global economy for centuries, are under threat. And Australia has become ground zero in this global battle.

items.title: Baby items, meal deliveries: ATO warns taxpayers to stop 'unusual' claims
items.description: The Australian Taxation Office (ATO) is warning Australians to stop claiming private expenses on their tax returns. The agency gives its tips this tax time, including the dos and don'ts of claiming work-related expenses and investment losses.

items.title: Former wife of tobacco baron alleges horrific life entangled in illegal trade
items.description: After an arranged marriage to tobacco baron Sam Albion, Kawther Salih says the relationship spiralled into an abusive situation that saw her subjugated into working in the underground tobacco industry.

items.title: Australia hits its highest number of billionaires on record. Do we need more?
items.description: Australia now has 178 billionaires — an increase of 17 from last year — who collectively hold more than $686 billion in wealth, sparking debate about the advantages and disadvantages of the growing number of ultra-wealthy.

items.title: Difference between buying new and used US submarines under AUKUS
items.description: Australia will only buy second-hand Virginia nuclear-powered submarines from the US during the AUKUS stopgap phase, with some analysts criticising the move and others believing it is a positive change of plan.

items.title: Workmate of missing Jack McLennan says he's 'given police absolutely everything'
items.description: The last known person to see missing Queensland man Jack McLennan alive has broken his public silence amid intense community speculation over his role in Mr McLennan's disappearance.

items.title: UK releases new documents on ex-US envoy Mandelson
items.description: Among the more than 1,000 pages of documents was a note from Peter Mandelson telling the UK foreign secretary at the time that the government would "never regret" giving him the job.

items.title: 'Happy [and safe] shooting!' AI chatbot's chilling message
items.description: An investigation into how AI chatbots respond to violent requests produces "deeply disturbing" results, as OpenAI denies ChatGPT encourage crime.

items.title: Parent 'thought it was a joke' upon hearing year 3 NAPLAN tests stolen
items.description: Dozens of primary school students are victims of an analogue data breach after their NAPLAN tests were stolen from a van in Melbourne's inner-north on April Fool's Day.

items.title: Real estate agency using fake AI salesperson to spam customers
items.description: "Daniel" is an AI real estate agent who calls strangers and secretly records conversations without their consent.

items.title: Antibiotic used by salmon farm detected 14 kilometres from treatment site
items.description: Tasmania's Natural Resources and Environment Department has confirmed the antibiotic florfenicol was detected at a 'low level' in wild seafood 14 kilometres from where the drug was administered.

items.title: Carly grew up in a cult. The experience partly inspired her latest show
items.description: Carly Sheppard is perhaps best known for experimental performance, but a coincidental meeting with a fellow dancer convinced her to go back to her roots.

items.title: Quiz: Are you smart enough to understand the Scripps Spelling Bee?
items.description: We don't think you'll have even heard of most of these words, never mind how to spell them.

items.title: Why make-up sex may not be fixing anything
items.description: Experts say if a fight keeps ending up in the bedroom, it could be a sign you and your partner aren't resolving anything.

items.title: Neighbours complain about 200 weekly chopper flights into luxury resort
items.description: A luxury resort that has been shut for three years hopes to reopen by chauffeuring guests down a steep 4WD track and flying them in on more than 200 helicopter flights a week.

items.title: Regional voters consider their options as One Nation popularity surges
items.description: Pauline Hanson's right-wing populist party is leading opinion polls for the first time, and regional Queenslanders say they can see why.

items.title: Chalmers accepts voters 'legitimate concerns' as One Nation overtakes Labor
items.description: Labor's federal budget is falling flat with its target demographic as millennials say they would rather vote for One Nation than Labor or the Greens, according to a new Redbridge poll.

items.title: 'Deeply concerning outbreak': Australia keeps borders open as Ebola spreads
items.description: The federal government will not impose border restrictions on travellers from Ebola-stricken countries despite new suspected cases in Italy and Brazil, as the worsening outbreak prompts other countries to take action.

items.title: Penguins return after feral cats culled from Little Dog Island
items.description: Penguins have been sighted on a remote Bass Strait island for the first time in decades after the successful eradication of feral cats and possums.

items.title: Miley Cyrus emails and emoji texts amid Melbourne film festival data leak
items.description: Melbourne International Film Festival customers receive strange texts and emails after a data breach linked to the event's third-party ticketing system.

items.title: Spotlight on Welcome to Country ceremonies in wake of Anzac Day controversy
items.description: Indigenous elders explain why they believe Welcome to Country ceremonies have faced opposition, and why abandoning the practice would create a cultural "abyss".

items.title: Teen charged with violent extremist offences allegedly planned school attack
items.description: Queensland Police say a 13-year-old boy posed an "imminent threat" to a Maryborough school.
